title: Exchange transformations presented by their adjuncts
statement: Let C, D, C′, D′ be categories, a : L ⊣ R and b : L′ ⊣ R′ adjunctions, G : C → C′ and H : D → D′ functors, and θ : G ⋙ L′ ≅ L ⋙ H a natural isomorphism. Using the adjunction hom equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], define squareExchange(a,b,G,H,θ) : R ⋙ G → H ⋙ R′ with component at N equal to b.homEquiv(θ(RN) followed by H(a.counit(N))). This is natural in N. Its inverse adjunct is θ(RN) followed by H(a.counit(N)), and it is equal as a natural transformation to unit insertion, squareTransport of θ, and counit contraction, with the canonical functor associators and unitors. This fixes the same exchange transformation by a presentation that exposes its adjoint without expanding the three composite steps.

proof.text: For h : N → M, apply the inverse b hom equivalence to the desired naturality equation. Naturality of that equivalence turns the equation into L′G(Rh) followed by θ(RM) and Hε(M), equal to θ(RN) followed by Hε(N) and Hh. Move Rh through θ by naturality; combine the H maps and apply naturality of the a counit. This proves naturality and constructs the displayed natural transformation without any choice.

The adjunct identity is the inverse-law of b.homEquiv. For equality with the original three-step exchange, use componentwise extensionality and injectivity of the inverse b hom equivalence. Expand the unit insertion, squareTransport and counit contraction at a component. Counit naturality moves the two R′ maps past the b counit; the b triangle identity cancels the inserted unit and counit. Both adjuncts are θ(RN) followed by Hε(N), so the transformations agree. The code proves this for arbitrary categories, including identity adjunctions and empty categories.
